# `deploy/compose/tls`

Serving certificate and private key for the tunnel gateway's connector
listener, plus the certificate authority that issued them.

**Nothing in this directory is committed.** It is generated by the end-to-end
script on the machine that runs the scenario, and it is key material for a
throwaway authority that exists for the duration of a test.

## What lands here

| File | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.crt` | `e2e/generate-secrets.sh` | `REVIEWPLANE_TUNNEL_TLS_CERT_FILE` |
| `gateway.key` | `e2e/generate-secrets.sh` | `REVIEWPLANE_TUNNEL_TLS_KEY_FILE` |
| `connector-ca.pem` | `e2e/run.sh` | `REVIEWPLANE_TUNNEL_CONNECTOR_CA_FILE`, `REVIEWPLANE_CONTROL_PLANE_CA_FILE` |

The two are produced at different times and by different authorities, which is
why the gateway is restarted partway through the scenario:

- `gateway.crt` and `gateway.key` are a self-signed pair for the internal
  origin, generated before anything starts. No public authority can issue for a
  reserved top-level domain, so the browser worker trusts this certificate by
  public-key pin rather than by chain (ADR-0015), and
  `generate-secrets.sh` writes that pin to `.env` as
  `REVIEWPLANE_TUNNEL_CERTIFICATE_SPKI`.
- `connector-ca.pem` is **exported from the running control plane**, which owns
  the authority that issues connector identities. It cannot exist before the
  control plane does, so `run.sh` fetches it from
  `GET /api/v1/connectors/certificate-authority` and recreates the gateway with
  it in place.

The gateway refuses to start unless all three of its settings name a readable
file (`services/tunnel-gateway/cmd/tunnel-gateway/main.go`), so a missing
certificate is a startup failure with a named setting rather than a listener
that quietly comes up without mutual TLS.

Everything here is mounted read-only at `/etc/reviewplane/tls` in the gateway
and in the `dev-fixture` container, both of which run as uid 10001. The files
are therefore mode 0644: the private key is protected by the directory not
being shared, not by its own mode. Do not copy that arrangement outside a test
deployment.

## Why `*.internal.invalid`

A browser reaches a published service at
`https://<public_alias>.internal.invalid/`
(`services/tunnel-gateway/README.md`). The serving certificate therefore needs a
subject alternative name covering `*.internal.invalid`, because the alias is
allocated per published service and is not known when the certificate is made.

`.invalid` is reserved by RFC 6761 and is guaranteed never to resolve in the
public DNS. That is the point: the internal origin cannot be confused with a
real name, and a certificate for it is worthless outside this deployment.

## Generating it

```bash
deploy/compose/e2e/generate-secrets.sh          # gateway.crt, gateway.key
deploy/compose/e2e/run.sh                       # connector-ca.pem, and the rest
```

`generate-secrets.sh` leaves an existing certificate alone; pass `--force` to
replace it. Regenerate rather than reuse across machines: these are test
certificates, and a long-lived private key sitting in a working tree is the
thing this directory is set up to prevent.

Do not hand-generate `connector-ca.pem`. The gateway verifies connector client
certificates against it, so it has to be the authority the control plane is
actually issuing from; a locally invented one produces a mutual-TLS handshake
failure at the point a connector opens its data channel, which is a long way
from the cause.

## Permissions and version control

`gateway.key` is a private key. Let the gateway read it through the read-only
mount rather than copying it into an image.

`.gitignore` at the repository root already excludes `deploy/compose/secrets/*`.
This directory needs its own entry — add the following if it is not present, so
that the only tracked files here are this README and `.gitkeep`:

```gitignore
deploy/compose/tls/*
!deploy/compose/tls/.gitkeep
!deploy/compose/tls/README.md
```

If a key is ever committed, rotating it is not optional and deleting the commit
is not sufficient: treat it as disclosed, regenerate the authority, and reissue
every certificate it signed.
